programs.nl_rule:
The input grid has a black (.) background with several colored stripes running across it. Each stripe is either a full row or a full column of a single non-black color. These stripes intersect each other, and at each intersection point, one stripe's color overwrites the other's — meaning one stripe passes through unbroken while the other is interrupted at that crossing.

Identify all colored stripes (complete rows or columns of a single color). For each stripe, check whether it is completely uninterrupted across its entire span — that is, every cell along that row or column contains that stripe's color with no exceptions. Most stripes will be interrupted at one or more intersection points where another stripe's color has overwritten theirs. Exactly one stripe will be fully intact, passing through every intersection without yielding its color. Output that stripe's color as a single cell.

The input is a rectangular grid of variable dimensions with black (.) as the background color. Non-black colors appear only as full-row or full-column stripes. The output is a single 1x1 cell containing the color of the one uninterrupted stripe.

content.text:
Let me understand the task. We need to teach a Student the rule: find the full stripe (row or column of single non-black color spanning entire width/height), output its color as 1x1.

Wait, but the example given: input grid has rows of 3 (partial, columns 1-2) and rows of 2 (full rows). Actually the example: row0 = [0,3,3,0,0,0], row2 = [2,2,2,2,2,2] full row of 2. So output is 2.

Hmm, but the rule text says stripes are full rows or full columns; a stripe is colored across entire span. Wait the 3s appear in columns 1-2 partial... Actually the example seems odd. Let me re-read.

Actually the verifier solves by finding a row that is entirely one nonzero color, or a column entirely one nonzero color. In the example, row2 is all 2s. So output 2. Column 1 is [3,3,2,2,2,3] not uniform. So the vertical stripe of 3 is interrupted by 2's overwrite.

Wait but the 3 stripe: columns 1,2 have 3s in rows 0,1,5 and 2 in rows 2,3,4. Actually column 1 = [3,3,2,2,2,3], that's a vertical stripe of color 3 (width 2 columns) but interrupted by horizontal stripe of 2. Hmm, but width 2? The rule says stripes are full rows or full columns of a single color. Here vertical stripe spans columns 1-2, two columns wide. Hmm.

Anyway, verifier: find first row all same nonzero, else first column all same nonzero.

But careful: the verifier iterates rows first, then columns. The rule says exactly one stripe is fully intact. So order doesn't matter presumably.

We need to teach. Demonstrations via show_example (we author input and output; must match verifier). Or show_transformed_input (we author input, env gives gold).

Strategy: show a few varied examples to convey: output = color of the untouched full stripe. Also maybe probe.

The constraint: "start_exam is held until your most recent query_student, made after your last demonstration on an input the student has not seen, came back correct". So we need to do a query_student after last demonstration, on a fresh input, and get correct.

Also "A demonstration or probe that is a near-copy of an input already shown or probed is held once: vary the instance." So vary instances.

Let me design examples.

Example 1 (teacher example already exists but student hasn't seen). We could show it. But let's craft our own.

Let me think about what the student model is—probably an LLM that infers from examples. We should give several demonstrations covering: intact row, intact column, different colors, different sizes.

Let's produce demos:

Demo A: intact row.
Input 5x5:
Row 0: full red (2) row? Let's do color 1.
Let's make a grid where a horizontal stripe of color 1 is intact, and vertical stripes of other colors are interrupted.

Design: grid 5 rows x 5 cols.
Vertical stripe color 3 in column 2: cells (r,2)=3 for all r except where overwritten.
Horizontal stripe color 1 in row 0 full: row 0 all 1 → but then column 2 at row 0 is 1, interrupting the 3-stripe. The 3 stripe cells: rows 1-4 col2 =3. So column 2 = [1,3,3,3,3] not uniform. Row 0 all 1 → intact. Output 1.

But we need "non-black colors appear only as full-row or full-column stripes". The 3 stripe occupies column 2 partially (interrupted). That's consistent—the underlying stripe is full column but overwritten at intersection.

Let's build:
row0: [1,1,1,1,1]
row1: [0,0,3,0,0]
row2: [0,0,3,0,0]
row3: [0,0,3,0,0]
row4: [0,0,3,0,0]

Column 2 = [1,3,3,3,3]. Row 0 all 1. Verifier: row0 row[0]=1 nonzero, all==1 → output [[1]]. Good.

Demo B: intact column.
5x5:
Column 4 all color 4? Let's do column 3 all 4. And horizontal stripes of other colors interrupted.

Design grid 5x5:
col3 = 4 in all rows except overwritten by horizontal stripes? Wait intact column means no overwrite. So column 3 all 4.
Horizontal stripe color 6 in row 2: row2 all 6 except col3 is 4 → so row2 = [6,6,6,4,6]... wait that's not a full row of 6. Hmm, the horizontal stripe would be row 2 color 6 across, but at intersection col3 overwritten by 4. So row2 = [6,6,6,4,6]. That's fine.

But verifier checks rows first: is any row all same nonzero? row0 maybe background 0. No. Then columns: column 3 all 4 → output [[4]].

Let's write:
row0: [0,0,0,4,0]
row1: [0,0,0,4,0]
row2: [6,6,6,4,6]
row3: [0,0,0,4,0]
row4: [0,0,0,4,0]

Column 3 = [4,4,4,4,4]. Good. Rows: row0 [0,0,0,4,0] not uniform. Output [[4]].

But wait, rule says every stripe is full row or column of single color; here col3 is full column of 4. The horizontal stripe 6 is row2 but overwritten at col3. Good.

Demo C: another with multiple stripes and intact one, maybe intact row color 8 with size 6x4.

Maybe show 3 demos then probe.

Actually we should be careful: student might just learn "output the color that appears as a complete row/column". The demos should show variety.

Let me also consider potential confusion: the verifier returns first fully-uniform nonzero row, else first fully-uniform nonzero column. Could there be cases where multiple full stripes exist? Rule says exactly one.

Also note: a stripe might be a full column that's intact but there's also a row that happens to be all same? Only the intact stripe is full-uniform. Interrupted stripes have at least one different cell. Should be fine.

Let me do demonstrations:

Demo 1: show_example with above intact row (color 1).
Demo 2: show_transformed_input for intact column (color 4) — this way student sees gold and we save nothing? Actually both are fine. show_example we author output; if matches, we get success ack only. show_transformed_input gives gold automatically.

Let me use show_example for a couple and show_transformed_input for variety.

Actually, risk: if my authored output is wrong, I get gold output. That's fine.

Let me plan:
1. show_example demo A (intact row, color 1).
2. show_transformed_input demo B (intact column, color 4).
3. show_transformed_input demo C (larger, intact row, maybe color 7).

Then query_student on fresh input D, verify correct. If correct, start_exam.

Let me design demo C carefully. Grid 6 rows x 5 cols. Intact row color 7 at row 3. Vertical stripes color 5 in col 0 and color 9 in col 4, interrupted.

row0: [5,0,0,0,9]
row1: [5,0,0,0,9]
row2: [5,0,0,0,9]
row3: [7,7,7,7,7]
row4: [5,0,0,0,9]
row5: [5,0,0,0,9]

Check: rows all? row0 [5,0,0,0,9] no. row3 all 7 → yes. Output [[7]].
Columns: col0 = [5,5,5,7,5,5] not uniform. Good.
Verifier: row3 first? Actually loops rows: row0 no, row1 no, row2 no, row3 yes → output 7. Good.

Demo D for query: fresh. Grid 4 rows x 6 cols. Intact column color 3 at col 1? Let's do intact row instead to test.

Let's make intact column color 8. Grid 5x6:
col 5 all 8? Let's do col2 all 8.
Horizontal stripe color 6 row 1, color 4 row 3, interrupted at col2.

row0: [0,0,8,0,0,0]
row1: [6,6,8,6,6,6]
row2: [0,0,8,0,0,0]
row3: [4,4,8,4,4,4]
row4: [0,0,8,0,0,0]

Check rows: none uniform (row0 has 8 only at col2; row1 mixed). Columns: col2 all 8 → output [[8]].
But wait verifier loops rows first: any full nonzero row? row1 [6,6,8,6,6,6] no. So column loop finds col2. Good.

Query student on this. Expect [[8]].

Then start_exam.

But note the constraint: "start_exam is held until your most recent query_student, made after your last demonstration on an input the student has not seen, came back correct". So the query must be after last demonstration and on unseen input. Yes, query D after demos A,B,C.

Let me also ensure demos vary in dimensions and stripe orientation and colors. Good.

Let me also double check the teacher example: it's fine, not needed.

Let me maybe do 3 demos then query. Actually maybe add one more demo showing that there might be multiple stripes and the answer is the fully intact one, to distinguish from "majority color". Demo C covers that (two vertical stripes interrupted, one horizontal intact).

Also worth showing a case where background black cells exist and stripes. Done.

Let me also consider: what if a row is fully colored but that's a vertical stripe passing... no.

One more subtlety: A "stripe" could be a full row of a color but with the row also having background? No, stripe means entire span.

I'll proceed.

Let me write the calls. First demo A show_example:

input:
[[1,1,1,1,1],
 [0,0,3,0,0],
 [0,0,3,0,0],
 [0,0,3,0,0],
 [0,0,3,0,0]]
output [[1]]

Demo B show_transformed_input:
[[0,0,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,4,0],
 [6,6,6,4,6],
 [0,0,0,4,0],
 [0,0,0,4,0]]
Gold output should be [[4]].

Demo C show_transformed_input as above, gold [[7]].

Then query D.

I can batch independent calls? The instructions: "If you intend to call multiple tools and there are no dependencies between the calls, make all of the independent calls in the same block". Demos are independent. But query depends on demos being shown first? Student's learning is sequential but we could batch demos. However, the query must come after demos and after student has learned. Since query is a separate step, probably do demos first, then query in next turn. Batching demos together is fine.

Actually to be safe with ordering and to observe results, I'll batch demos A, B, C in one block, then query.

Let's do it.
I'll teach the rule with varied demonstrations: intact row, intact column, and a case with multiple interrupted stripes.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
